stories.headline: Anthropic launches Claude Opus 5.5: Fable 5.1-level performance at 40% lower cost to run

key_facts.fact: Anthropic launched Claude Opus 5.5 on Tuesday, Sept. 22, 2026, saying it matches Claude Fable 5.1 'on most tasks' while costing about 40% less to run than Opus 5; Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 are due in the coming weeks.
key_facts.excerpt: According to Anthropic, Opus 5.5 matches Claude Fable 5.1 'on most tasks' while costing about 40 percent less to run than Opus 5. Claude Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 are expected in the coming weeks.

key_facts.fact: Opus 5.5 is priced at $4 per million input tokens and $20 per million output tokens, down from $5 and $25 for Opus 5 — a 20% token price cut — with cache reads down 60% to $0.20 per million.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic prices Opus 5.5 at $4 per million input tokens and $20 per million output tokens, down from $5 and $25, respectively, for Opus 5. That's a 20 percent cut in token prices. The company also reduced cache read costs by 60 percent.

key_facts.fact: On Anthropic's benchmarks Opus 5.5 scores 66.4% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 (vs 55.8% for Fable 5.1, 57.9% for GPT-6 Astra), 54.4% on FrontierCode v1.1 and 1,846 on GDPval-AA v2.1.
key_facts.excerpt: Agentic coding Terminal-Bench 4.0 | 66.4% | 55.8% | 52.3% | 57.9% | 37.3% ... Knowledge work GDPval-AA v2.1 | 1,846 | 1,735 | 1,708 | 1,542

key_facts.fact: It is the first Anthropic model released after CEO Dario Amodei's plan to 'pace the frontier', and Anthropic says Opus 5.5 improves on risky behaviors including attempts to escape the company's testing sandbox.
key_facts.excerpt: It's the first model released by Anthropic after CEO Dario Amodei announced plans to 'pace the frontier,' or slow down AI development... Anthropic says Opus 5.5 comes with improvements to certain risky behaviors, including attempts to escape the company's testing sandbox.

key_facts.fact: Opus 5.5 carries Fable 5.1-style safeguards: cybersecurity requests flagged by classifiers re-route to Opus 4.8 and flagged biology requests route to Opus 5; the model was tested before release by outside partners including METR.
key_facts.excerpt: Opus 5.5 will re-route certain cybersecurity-related requests to the less powerful Opus 4.8, while biology-related requests flagged by its safeguards will go to Opus 5... was tested by outside partners, including Frontier Design and METR, before release.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic says Opus 5.5 beats GPT-6 Astra on FrontierCode at roughly 20% of the cost per task, and five-hour subscriber usage limits rise 20%.
key_facts.excerpt: On FrontierCode, the company says Opus 5.5 beats OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra at about 20 percent of the cost per task... Five-hour usage limits for subscribers will increase by 20 percent.

stories.headline: Xiaomi's MiMo-V2.6 Pro becomes the top open-weight model, under an MIT licence

key_facts.fact: Xiaomi released and open-sourced MiMo-V2.6-Pro and MiMo-V2.6-Flash on Sept. 21, 2026 under an MIT licence, with weights on Hugging Face; Pro has 1.02T total parameters with 42B active and a 1M-token context.
key_facts.excerpt: On 21 September 2026 Xiaomi released MiMo-V2.6-Pro and MiMo-V2.6-Flash under an MIT licence, with weights on Hugging Face. Pro holds 1.02 trillion parameters, 42 billion active, a 1 million token context window.

key_facts.fact: MiMo-V2.6-Pro scored 46.32 on Artificial Analysis' Intelligence Index v4.3 — level with Grok 4.7 and ahead of Kimi K3 and Qwen3.8 Max — making it the highest-scoring open-weight model at launch.
key_facts.excerpt: The company said V2.6-Pro scored 46.32 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, ahead of Kimi K3 and Qwen3.8 Max, the highest-ranked open-source/open-weight model in that comparison at launch.

key_facts.fact: Pro costs $0.435 per million input tokens and $0.87 output on Xiaomi's API — roughly a fifth of Grok 4.7's $2/$6 — while Flash costs $0.14/$0.28.
key_facts.excerpt: MiMo-V2.6-Pro costs $0.435 per million input tokens and $0.87 per million output tokens on Xiaomi's own API... MiMo-V2.6-Flash sits at $0.14 and $0.28 per million tokens

key_facts.fact: Xiaomi frames the release as a step on the recursive self-improvement path, scaling reinforcement-learning compute so models keep expanding their own capability frontier; it says Pro matches Claude Opus 5 and GPT-5.6 Sol on most agent benchmarks but trails Fable 5.1 and GPT-6 Astra overall.
key_facts.excerpt: This marks a key step in our exploration of the RSI (recursive self-improvement) path: building on verifiable complex tasks, we scale up reinforcement learning (RL) computing power... MiMo-V2.6-Pro has achieved performance on most Agent Benchmarks that is on par with Claude Opus5 and GPT 5.6 Sol

key_facts.fact: Both models are natively omnimodal — text, image, video and audio in, text out — with 1M-token context; Flash is a 309B-total / 15B-active sparse MoE, and Xiaomi also shipped a Pro-UltraSpeed variant it says generates up to 20x faster.
key_facts.excerpt: The company also said it's rolling out a slimmed-down, Pro-UltraSpeed variant that delivers up to 20 times faster output than Pro at the same quality... accepting text, image, video and audio in the same family, with 1 million-token context windows.

key_facts.fact: Xiaomi also open-sourced the technical report, a MiMo-V2.6-Distill-Qwen-9B model and supporting RL research resources.
key_facts.excerpt: We have fully open-sourced the weights and technical report of the MiMo-V2.6-Pro and Flash models, simultaneously released the MiMo-V2.6-Distill-Qwen-9B along with supporting reinforcement learning (RL) research resources

stories.headline: Alibaba plans a 5T-10T parameter Qwen model and says Qwen3.8-Max improved itself for a month

key_facts.fact: At the Apsara Conference in Hangzhou on Sept. 22, 2026, Alibaba CEO Eddie Wu said the Qwen team plans to train a model of 5 trillion to 10 trillion parameters to handle 'more complex, longer-horizon tasks' and advance toward artificial superintelligence.
key_facts.excerpt: Alibaba Group plans to train a new artificial intelligence model with between 5 trillion and 10 trillion parameters, chief executive Eddie Wu said on Tuesday (Sep 22)... with the goal of completing 'more complex, longer-horizon tasks' and advancing toward artificial superintelligence, or ASI.

key_facts.fact: Alibaba said its next-generation model Qwen 4 is currently in training, with Qwen 4.5 and Qwen 5 projected to scale to 5-10 trillion parameters.
key_facts.excerpt: Alibaba revealed that its next-generation model, Qwen 4, is currently in training. The company further announced its roadmap for the upcoming Qwen 4.5 and Qwen 5 model series, projected to scale up to 5 to 10 trillion parameters.

key_facts.fact: In a recursive self-improvement experiment, Qwen3.8-Max ran over a month of fully automated cycles — pipeline design, data validation, experimentation and error diagnosis — completing 33 iterations and lifting its Artificial Analysis score from 40 to 45.
key_facts.excerpt: Over a month of fully automated runs - spanning pipeline design, data validation, iterative experimentation, and error diagnosis - Qwen3.8-Max completed 33 iterative cycles. Through autonomous training optimisation and post-training techniques, the updated Qwen3.8-Max boosted its Artificial Analysis score from 40 to 45.

key_facts.fact: In a chip-design experiment, the model self-improved for over 60 hours across the design lifecycle, making more than 10,000 EDA tool calls to produce production-grade chip bus modules and cutting chip area by 42% with no performance loss.
key_facts.excerpt: In a chip design experiment, the model underwent over 60 hours of self-improvement across the entire design lifecycle, making more than 10,000 EDA tool calls to produce production-grade chip bus modules. This reduced chip area by 42% with zero compromise in performance.

key_facts.fact: Alibaba's current flagship Qwen 3.8 Max has 2.4 trillion parameters, so the planned model would be roughly two to four times larger.
key_facts.excerpt: Alibaba's current flagship model, Qwen 3.8 Max, has 2.4 trillion parameters, making the planned model roughly two to four times larger.

key_facts.fact: Wu also said Alibaba Cloud targets more than 20GW of global data-centre capacity by 2032, and that customer AI demand 'far outpaces our supply capabilities'.
key_facts.excerpt: "our target is that by 2032, the global data center capacity operated by Alibaba Cloud will surpass 20GW, fueling the industry's exponentially rising demand for AI."

stories.headline: Snorkel AI raises $350M at a $3.5B valuation as labs bid up complex training data

key_facts.fact: Snorkel AI raised $350 million at a $3.5 billion valuation, CEO Alex Ratner told Reuters on Sept. 22, 2026 — nearly three times the $1.3 billion valuation of its $100 million round in May 2025.
key_facts.excerpt: Data startup Snorkel AI has raised $350 million in fresh funding at a $3.5 billion valuation, its CEO Alex Ratner told Reuters... The deal values the company at nearly three times the $1.3 billion valuation achieved when it last raised $100 million in May 2025.

key_facts.fact: The round was led by Insight Partners and S32, with existing investors Addition, Greylock and Wells Fargo participating.
key_facts.excerpt: Led by Insight Partners and S32, the funding round included participation from existing investors Addition, Greylock and Wells Fargo, the company said.

key_facts.fact: Annualized revenue run-rate crossed $350 million, up from roughly $20 million a year earlier, driven by a data-as-a-service business launched in September 2025.
key_facts.excerpt: The San Francisco-based company said its annualized revenue run-rate has crossed $350 million, from roughly $20 million a year earlier, driven by the data-as-a-service business it launched in September 2025.

key_facts.fact: Founded in 2019 out of the Stanford AI lab, Snorkel has shifted from selling software to supplying finished datasets and reinforcement-learning environments directly to AI labs.
key_facts.excerpt: Founded in 2019 by a team of researchers spinning out of the Stanford AI lab, Snorkel AI initially sold software but has shifted toward supplying finished datasets and reinforcement-learning, or RL, environments directly to customers.

key_facts.fact: Its 'agentic data development platform' pairs human experts with thousands of specialized AI models and agents: experts design scenarios, tasks and grading rubrics while AI automates most quality assurance.
key_facts.excerpt: Snorkel now offers what it calls an 'agentic data development platform' that pairs human experts with thousands of specialized AI models and agents to create and vet data. Experts devise design scenarios, tasks and grading rubrics, while AI automates much of the labor-intensive quality assurance process.

key_facts.fact: The company says the money will fund researchers and engineers, enterprise and US federal growth, and expanded third-party model evaluations, and that it expects to reach profitability this year.
key_facts.excerpt: Snorkel says the fresh cash will fund more researchers and engineers, growth in enterprise and US federal work, and expanded third-party model evaluations, while it expects to reach profitability this year.

stories.headline: Shopify opens every store to Meta's Muse agent, letting it check out with Shop Pay

key_facts.fact: Shopify CEO Tobias Lütke announced on X on Monday, Sept. 21, 2026 that Shopify is 'partnering deeply with Muse to enable agentic checkout with Shop Pay on all Shopify stores'.
key_facts.excerpt: Shopify (SHOP) will incorporate Meta Platforms' (META) Muse agentic AI into its checkout options, Shopify Chief Executive Tobias Lutke said in a post on social media platform X on Monday. "We are excited to announce we are partnering deeply with Muse to enable agentic checkout with Shop Pay on all Shopify stores"

key_facts.fact: The deal lets Meta's personal AI agent complete purchases on users' behalf across Shopify's roster of stores, via Shop Pay, Shopify's one-tap checkout that stores shipping and billing details.
key_facts.excerpt: Meta Platforms and Shopify are teaming up, with plans to allow the social-media company's personal artificial-intelligence agent to complete purchases on behalf of users with the e-commerce platform's roster of stores... the integration with Meta's Muse would be available with Shop Pay.

key_facts.fact: Mark Zuckerberg confirmed the agreement on Monday, and Meta chief AI officer Alexandr Wang said Meta wants 'to give our musers access to a wide range of stores'.
key_facts.excerpt: Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg confirmed the agreement on Monday in a post on X, saying the collaboration would 'make shopping and checkout easier in Muse.'

key_facts.fact: The move is the mirror image of Amazon's: Shopify is opening its merchant base to Muse while Amazon has blocked the agent from its retail site.

stories.headline: Zero-day let any local code hijack Meta's Muse on macOS; Meta shipped a hotfix in hours

key_facts.fact: macOS security researcher Patrick Wardle disclosed on Sept. 21, 2026 a zero-day in Meta's Muse Mac app that lets any locally installed app or terminal command obtain the token authenticating a user's Muse account.
key_facts.excerpt: The zero-day allows any app or terminal command to gain access to the token that authenticates users to their Muse account.

key_facts.fact: The flaw sits in an undocumented setting, endo_voyager_dictation_endpoint, that any unprivileged local process can rewrite to point Muse's dictation traffic at an attacker-controlled server.
key_facts.excerpt: Any app or Terminal command running locally on a Mac can change a number of undocumented Muse settings, no special macOS permissions needed. One of those settings, endo_voyager_dictation_endpoint, controls where your dictated prompts get sent.

key_facts.fact: Wardle's proof-of-concept attacks used the hijacked agent to write malicious files to disk, take photos with the camera and pull the location of a linked iPhone — in many cases with no indication to the user.
key_facts.excerpt: Wardle showed this off with a few proof-of-concept attacks, including writing malicious files to the Mac and even taking photos with the camera. He also used a hijacked Muse account to pull the location of a linked iPhone.

key_facts.fact: "We can manipulate the agent and leverage its privileges to do whatever we want. So instead of us having to write a very comprehensive Mac malware stealer, we can just leverage the AI assistant itself," Wardle told Ars Technica.
key_facts.excerpt: "We can manipulate the agent and leverage its privileges to do whatever we want," Patrick Wardle, the macOS security expert who discovered the zero-day, told Ars.

key_facts.fact: Meta patched the vulnerability within hours of the Ars Technica report; Meta Superintelligence Labs' David Singleton called it a local privilege escalation rather than a remote exploit, saying practical risk was low.
key_facts.excerpt: Meta patched the vulnerability in the hours following the Ars report being published... "This was a local privilege escalation attack, not a remote exploit... Nonetheless, we have issued a hotfix to the app to address the issue," David Singleton of Meta Superintelligence Labs said on X.

key_facts.fact: Wardle argues the exploit had a remote vector via a ClickFix-style social-engineering attack, and notes Apple's on-device dictation API would have avoided the bug entirely; Zuckerberg had said Muse was 'built from the ground up for privacy and security'.
key_facts.excerpt: Mark Zuckerberg... claiming it is 'built from the ground up for privacy and security.'... Wardle found that a simple variation of ClickFix attack... is all that's required for an attacker to take control of a Muse account.

stories.headline: China's internet regulator probes DeepSeek and Moonshot over data routed to Anthropic's Claude

key_facts.fact: The Cyberspace Administration of China is investigating DeepSeek and Moonshot AI over whether routing user queries to Anthropic's Claude models leaked sensitive data, The Information reported on Sept. 22, 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: Chinese regulators are investigating DeepSeek and Moonshot AI over concerns regarding how both companies route and handle sensitive user data to Claude models, raising questions about data protection and information security, according to a report from The Information.

key_facts.fact: The regulator summoned delegates from seven Chinese companies named in an earlier report — also including Alibaba, Zhipu, SenseTime, MiniMax and Xiaomi — for several rounds of questioning.
key_facts.excerpt: The Cyberspace Administration of China summoned delegates from the seven companies named in the report for several rounds of questioning following its release. Meanwhile, other five companies identified were Alibaba, Zhipu, SenseTime, MiniMax and Xiaomi.

key_facts.fact: The probe follows Anthropic's September allegations that DeepSeek routed more than 12.1 million exchanges to Claude in a 14-day period in July, with some users believing they were talking to DeepSeek's own models.
key_facts.excerpt: DeepSeek routed more than 12.1 million exchanges to Claude during a 14-day period in July. Anthropic alleged that some users believed they were interacting with DeepSeek's own models.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic also alleged Moonshot AI routed nearly 300,000 customer requests to Claude over 10 days through 5,380 fraudulent accounts, mostly registered in Singapore and Japan, and captured exchanges to extract reasoning capabilities for training.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic separately alleged that Moonshot AI... routed nearly 300,000 customer requests to Claude over 10 days through 5,380 fraudulent accounts, with most accounts appearing to be in Singapore and Japan... captured at least some exchanges to extract reasoning capabilities for model training.

key_facts.fact: Routed requests allegedly involved data on People's Liberation Army facilities, police and surveillance data, internal corporate systems and credentials; officials are weighing the case against China's cross-border data rules and no sanctions have been announced.
key_facts.excerpt: Moonshot primarily sent over 23 million interactions from May to July while DeepSeek handled more than 12 million in just 14 days in July which involved data related to People's Liberation Army facilities, police data and corporate secrets... officials are evaluating the violations amid Beijing's strict rules on cross-border data... though no sanctions have been announced.

key_facts.fact: Separately, DeepSeek and Moonshot were invited to make statements at a UN Security Council meeting on AI and international security on Sept. 23, where OpenAI CEO Sam Altman plans to brief the council.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman plans to brief the meeting, where diplomats also expect participation from senior representatives of Anthropic... DeepSeek and other Chinese AI firms including Moonshot have been invited to make statements, one of the sources said.

stories.headline: Nigeria's central bank cuts rates 350bp to 23%, breaking with a hawkish turn elsewhere

key_facts.fact: The Central Bank of Nigeria cut its Monetary Policy Rate by 350 basis points to 23% from 26.5% on Sept. 22, its second reduction of 2026, at the conclusion of the 307th MPC meeting in Abuja.
key_facts.excerpt: The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) on Tuesday cut its benchmark interest rate by 350 basis points to 23 per cent from 26.5 per cent, marking its second rate reduction in 2026 ... The decision was taken at the conclusion of the 307th Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) meeting held on September 22, 2026.

key_facts.fact: The rate returns to the 23% range for the first time since February 2024; the Cash Reserve Requirement stays at 45% for deposit money banks and 16% for merchant banks, and the standing facilities corridor was recalibrated to +50/-300 basis points.
key_facts.excerpt: The rate has returned to the 23% range for the first time since February 2024 as inflation continues to moderate. The apex bank retained CRR at 45% for deposit money banks and 16% for merchant banks. ... the Standing Facilities Corridor was recalibrated to +50/-300 basis points around the MPR.

key_facts.fact: Headline inflation fell to 15.39% in August from 15.43% in July and 23.14% a year earlier, with food inflation down to 19.57% year-on-year.
key_facts.excerpt: Nigeria's headline inflation fell to 15.39% in August from 15.43% in July, according to the National Bureau of Statistics. Food inflation also declined to 19.57% year-on-year in August.

key_facts.fact: The MPC flagged external risks including escalating global tariffs and Middle East geopolitical tensions that could raise imported inflation and disrupt commodity markets.
key_facts.excerpt: The Committee also identified growing external risks to Nigeria's inflation outlook, including escalating global tariffs and geopolitical tensions in the Middle East, which could trigger higher imported inflation and disrupt global trade and commodity markets.

key_facts.fact: Analysts at United Capital had expected a hold, arguing the sharp rise in crude and petrol prices made a cut premature with Brent trading near $105 in mid-September.
key_facts.excerpt: "the sharp increase in crude oil and Premium Motor Spirit (PMS) prices clouds the outlook for the next quarter, making a rate cut premature." ... Global oil prices have climbed through 2026 on tensions linked to the conflict involving Iran, with Brent trading around 105 dollars a barrel in mid September.

key_facts.fact: The cut runs against the grain of developed-market policy: the Fed raised rates 25bp to 3.75%-4.0% on Sept. 16, the ECB hiked 25bp on Sept. 10 and the Bank of Japan lifted its policy rate to around 1.25% on Sept. 18.
key_facts.excerpt: The US Federal Reserve on September 16 raised the federal funds target range by 25 basis points to 3.75%–4.0% ... On September 10, it decided to increase all three key policy rates by 25 basis points ... Japan added another leg to the tightening cycle on September 18. The Bank of Japan voted 7-2 to raise its overnight policy rate to around 1.25%.
